instructions: Cut each chicken breast in half horizontally so you have 4 thin cutlets, one for each roll. Lay them between sheets of plastic wrap and pound them to about 1/4 inch thick.
Make the sauce. Grate the onion into a saucepan with the 2 tbsp olive oil, then mince the garlic. Set the pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes, until it's soft.

Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Add the tomato sauce, 1 tbsp of the Italian seasoning, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp sugar. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Taste it and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Turn the heat to low to keep it warm.

Set up three shallow dishes. Put the flour in the first, the beaten eggs in the second, and the panko in the third. Stir the Parmesan, the remaining 1 tbsp Italian seasoning and 1 tsp salt into the panko.
Pat the cutlets dry. Coat each one in the flour, then the egg, then press it firmly into the panko on both sides.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat until a pinch of panko sizzles right away. Fry 2 cutlets at a time for 4 minutes on the first side, until deep golden. Flip them and cook the other side for 4 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest cutlet there. No thermometer? Cut into the center of one: it's done when there's no pink left. Transfer the cutlets to a paper towel lined plate.
Heat the broiler to high with the rack in the middle. Split the rolls and set them open on a baking sheet.
Put a cutlet on the bottom half of each roll. Spoon about 1/4 cup of the sauce over each cutlet and top with 1/2 cup of the mozzarella.
Broil for 3 to 5 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Watch closely, since the rolls toast quickly.
Scatter the basil over the top, close the sandwiches and serve with the rest of the warm sauce.
To make the cutlets ahead, fry them, cool them and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Warm them on a rack in a 400°F oven for 10 minutes, then assemble and broil. Keep the sauce in a separate container.
method_notes: All three bread cutlets in flour, egg and crumbs with Parmesan, then top them with marinara and melted mozzarella on a toasted roll. The lead (Tasting Table, 5.0 from 21) fries panko cutlets and makes a quick onion and garlic tomato sauce, which this follows; DeLallo and Real Food with Sarah bake the cutlets instead. The dairy-free tag is dropped for this dish because Parmesan and mozzarella are what make it chicken Parmesan; nut-free is kept.
